name: Penny 5-1-5 Bracket Coverage vs Condensed Bunch
formation: Penny 5-1-5 Front vs 11P Gun 3x1 Condensed Bunch
coverage: Box / Triangle Bracket Match vs 3x1 Bunch
frontName: Penny 5-1-5 Front (5 on line, 1 ILB, 5 DBs)

summary.motive: Eliminate natural pick and rub routes from condensed bunch sets by employing a 3-over-2 Triangle Bracket match coverage while retaining a disciplined 4-man Penny rush.
summary.keyDefender: STAR (inside bracket DB) & FS (top cap safety)
summary.whyItWorks: Offenses use condensed bunches to create free releases against man coverage. Triangle matching plays zone distribution based on route directions (in, out, up), eliminating picks entirely.
summary.failureMode: A deep scissors or post-corner combination by the bunch if the safety hesitates between two vertical stems.

beats.title: Penny 5-1-5 Front & Triangle Bracket Pre-Snap
beats.text: Chris Shula deploys a 5-man Penny front with a 3-over-2 "Box/Triangle" bracket over the condensed 3x1 bunch, featuring STAR (inside), RCB (outside), and FS (top).

beats.title: Triangle Rules Distribute Bunch Releases
beats.text: As the bunch releases, the defense seamlessly sorts the routes without getting picked: RCB jumps the flat (Y), STAR clamps the shallow in-cut (H), and FS caps the vertical wheel (Z).

beats.title: Natural Rubs Neutralized; All Windows Clamped
beats.text: The offense’s designed pick-plays are completely countered by zone distribution rules. The QB is forced to hold the ball as all three bunch receivers are suffocated.

beats.title: 4-Man Penny Front Sacks QB
beats.text: With nowhere to deliver the football, 4iR breaks free from the interior rush to combine with LOLB for the third-down coverage sack.

relations.tell: Penny 5-1-5 front with STAR, corner, and safety forming a tight triangle bracket over the condensed bunch to exchange routes in-and-out
